content.text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- **Morpholine:** a six-membered ring with one O and one N. The N carries a CH2CH2 chain.
- **Linker:** the chain ends in an O that attaches to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Pyridine:** the benzene's para carbon bonds to a pyridine ring at the position meta to N, which is C5 of the pyridine (the ring N is at the bottom right). C2 of the pyridine, next to N, carries a CH2.
- **Amide:** that CH2 connects to C(=O)NH, and the NH bears a benzyl group (CH2 on a phenyl ring).

Pyridine ring atoms: C2 (bearing CH2), N1, C6 (an aromatic CH), C5 (bearing the aryl group), C4 and C3.

In the image, the ring runs from the carbon bonded to the aryl group (left, at about 735,640), up to the top-left carbon (778,567), across to the top-right carbon (865,570), and down to the carbon bearing the CH2 (905,646). From there it goes to N (860,720), then to the bottom-left carbon (778,718), and back to the aryl-bearing carbon. So the aryl carbon is bonded to the CH next to N (C6) and to a CH (C4). The aryl carbon is therefore C5 and the CH2-bearing carbon is C2, which matches the assignment above.

SMILES: O=C(Cc1ccc(cn1)-c1ccc(OCCN2CCOCC2)cc1)NCc1ccccc1
